pages.title: CPS
pages.text: The $(item)Radio Programmer$() floppy installs $(thing)CPS$(), the programming software radio shops use. It reads and writes the channels of a $(l:radiocraft:radios/commercial_radios)commercial radio$(): 16, or 40 on the upgraded handheld (the list scrolls; A, B and C mark where each zone starts).$(br2)A mobile radio already placed is reached by its programming cable: touching the computer, or on its $(l:radiocraft:radios/data_wire)data wire$(). F5 reads it, F6 writes it.

pages.title: Program radios
pages.text: Handhelds, and mobiles still in item form, are programmed by hand. $(thing)F9$() turns on the $(thing)Program radios$() mode; $(thing)Close$() (or C) leaves the screen with CPS still in that mode.$(br2)Now hold the radio (main hand, or off hand with the main hand empty) and right click the computer or its monitor: the channels on screen are written into it. $(thing)Sneak$() and right click to read the radio into CPS instead. The mode ends when CPS is closed, another program opened, the power goes, or after five minutes unused.

Enter edits a channel: its name (8 letters), receive and transmit frequencies (transmit blank for simplex, RX for receive only), FM or DIG, a CTCSS tone, and on digital channels an encryption key with whether it may be read back. Del clears one, Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V copy one. A write is all or nothing, and the radio refuses what it cannot do (a frequency out of its bands, digital on the basic brick).

pages.title: Unit IDs
pages.text: Every commercial radio sends its $(thing)unit ID$() (1-9999) each time it keys up: a short data burst on FM, inside the data on digital. Radios with a display show who is talking, by ID or by the name in their $(thing)contact list$(). $(thing)F4$() sets the ID CPS writes; programming radios by hand, it goes up by one after each radio. Left at 0, each radio keeps its own (a new radio gets one). $(thing)F7$() edits the contact list.

pages.title: Hidden keys
pages.text: A key set as not readable shows as $(thing)****$(): it never comes off the radio. Write the channels back and the radio keeps its own key; type a new key over it to change it. A hidden key cannot be copied to another radio.$(br2)Ctrl+S saves the channels as a $(thing)codeplug$() (.CPG) to load into other radios of the fleet; a 40-channel codeplug loaded for a 16-channel radio leaves out what does not fit. F8 erases a wired radio back to factory blank.
A blank floppy and a comparator.
